summary.text: St. Theodota raised the unmercenary physicians Sts. Cosmas and Damian in Christian faith after their father’s death.

blocks.text: The OCA identifies St. Theodota as the mother of the unmercenary physicians Sts. Cosmas and Damian. Its short life describes the family as natives of Asia Minor, although the familiar calendar title associates her sons with Mesopotamia. Her husband died while the children were young.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The account emphasizes her example and her reading of sacred books to the children. The Greek Archdiocese adds that she arranged a broad education for them, especially in medicine. Their later care of the sick without taking payment explains the title unmercenaries. The sources thus remember her through the Christian formation and education of her household.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: These short entries do not establish the circumstances or exact date of St. Theodota’s death. They do not identify this mother as a martyr. She must not be confused with other women called Theodota or Theodote who appear in separate martyrdom narratives.
